facts.statement: The study used a cross-sectional survey format to collect data from members of the International League Against Epilepsy between February and May 2025.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants were presented with five clinical scenarios involving acute symptomatic seizures caused by stroke, head injury, meningitis, low sodium levels, or alcohol withdrawal.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Out of 963 doctors from 92 countries, about 62% said they would start seizure medication for visible seizures, while 61% would do so for seizures seen only on brain scans.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Doctors' decisions varied widely, with the most disagreement occurring for seizures caused by alcohol withdrawal and for seizures detected only by monitoring equipment.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Among 291 doctors who treat newborns, 75% said they would continue seizure medication after the baby left the hospital.
facts.subject: humans
